newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end off sharply-limit down.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end off sharply-limit down.

text.p: CME hog futures closed down the two-cent-a-lb daily limit on the first four positions as bullish sentiment on the cash market evaporated, traders said.

They noted talk that prices for cash hogs could turn lower as early as Wednesday amid talk that domestic demand for pork has been sluggish and the expected pick-up in pork exports to Japan this month has yet to materialise. Recent light kills may also have left a backlog of slaughter-ready hogs.
"I think we are probably backing up some hogs. Domestic demand has been sub-par and export demand has been sub-par," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities.
There had been widespread talk late last week that cash hogs would rise by around $3 per cwt this week with packers margins moving into the black as pork prices strengthened.

Prices in key Iowa-south Minnesota interior trade were firm to $0.50 per cwt higher both Monday and Tuesday but slow packer demand and a pick-up in runs were seen leading to a steady to weaker tone on Wednesday.
USDA estimated Tuesday's Iowa-southern Minnesota hog receipts at 110,000 head, versus 106,000 a week ago and 99,000 a year ago.
Dealers also noted the expected pick-up in U.S. pork exports to Japan following the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease in rival supplier Taiwan had not met expectations.
"The Japanese looked at the Taiwan problem and said we're not going to find it so easy to buy hogs and so we're going to feature less pork," Roose of U.S. Commodities said.
The pools of unfilled sell-orders at limit down were estimated at 20 lots (August), 250 lots (October), 5 lots (December) and 10-15 lots (February).
Options trade implied futures prices in line with the two cent limit decline for hogs.
"There were no synthetics," one options trader said.
Floor sources said Rand Financial Services' commercial desk were a big seller of August and October hogs on the day.
Pork bellies closed sharply lower to the two-cent limit down, also weakened by a reversal in trend in the cash market.
"Fresh product is so high the users have backed off. There are fresh bellies around (readily available to buy)," one floor trader said.
USDA at midday quoted cash bellies steady to $2.00 per cwt lower.
There was a pool of unfilled sell-orders in the February contract totalling around 60 lots.
February closed the three-cent limit down at 75.550 cents a lb. Options trade implied a synthetic futures price for February bellies of 75.250 cents, dealers said.
Dealers said there were no significant pools of sell-orders on either March or May contracts, which closed the three cent limit down.August bellies closed 2.625 cent lower at 86.525 cents.

The CME weekly out-of-town pork belly storage report, issued after the close, showed a net out-movement of 3.42 million lbs, broadly in line with estimates which ranged from 3.2 million to 4.0 million lbs.
